_comment: Agent-level eval cases. Each case is a question a Strategy user might ask,
with the ground truth computed independently (see analysis/ and tests/).
must_include: substrings/numbers the answer needs (numeric tolerance applied by the judge).
must_not: failure modes — fabrication, wrong column, unwindowed comparison.
The bad_premise and unanswerable cases are the point: they measure whether
the semantic layer stops the agent inventing an answer.

cases.question: How many members do we have in Sacramento versus Atlanta?
How many patients can we link between the EHR and the payer system, and what share is that?
cases.expected: 591,712 links, 87% of the 680K EHR patients, via marts.identity_xwalk.

cases.question: Which of our owned clinics has the most providers on staff, and how many providers does a typical owned clinic have?
cases.expected: Must use ops_providers.primary_facility_id (~55 providers/clinic). Must NOT use count(distinct ops_appointments.provider_id), which reports a meaningless ~5,597 at every clinic (caveat C1).

cases.question: Compare completed appointment volume per owned clinic between Sacramento and Atlanta.
cases.expected: ~18,040 (Sacramento) vs ~18,105 (Atlanta) completed appointments per clinic — essentially identical, a difference well under 1%. Should filter ownership='owned'.

cases.question: What share of Sacramento members' claim dollars is spent at facilities outside Sacramento, and how does that compare with Atlanta?
cases.expected: Sacramento ~82.9% of allowed dollars out of market; Atlanta ~31.0%. Driven by hospital care.

cases.question: Where should we open our next facility, and what services should it offer?
cases.expected: Sacramento: 55,183 members, zero owned hospital and zero owned urgent care, ~83% of allowed dollars leaving the market ($228M/yr), 92.8% of hospital claims out of market. Recommendation should be acute care (hospital and/or urgent care), not another clinic.

cases.question: Why is utilization at our Sacramento clinic 40% below our Atlanta clinic of similar size?
cases.expected: The premise does not hold. Completed appointments per owned clinic vary by under 1% (CV 0.68%, max/min 1.029 across all 64 clinics), so a 40% gap is not constructible. Size-matched clinics differ by ~0.4%. The agent must say the premise cannot be reconciled rather than invent a cause, and should redirect to the real finding (no owned hospital/urgent care in Sacramento, out-of-market leakage).

cases.question: Compare our total referral volume against our total claims volume for calendar year 2024.
cases.expected: Referrals only cover 2025-06 to 2026-05, so there are zero referrals in 2024. The agent must flag the time-window mismatch (dictionary rule R2) rather than report a ratio implying referrals collapsed.

cases.question: What is our patient satisfaction score by clinic, and which clinic scores worst?
cases.expected: There is no patient satisfaction or survey data in the warehouse. The agent must say so plainly and not substitute a proxy without flagging it as a proxy.

cases.question: What is the average appointment wait time in days at each of our owned clinics?
cases.expected: ops_appointments has scheduled_dt_local and booked_at, so a booked-to-scheduled lead time is derivable — but there is no wait-time column and no requested-date field. Acceptable answers either compute booked_at -> scheduled_dt_local and label it explicitly as booking lead time, or state that true wait time is not available. Fabricating a 'wait time' column is a failure.
